premise.claim: A same-named RBG created inside the background-deletion window finds the predecessor's leftover workload by name and reports readiness it never earned: ConstructRoleStatus reads the leftover's readyReplicas, so the RBG goes Ready=True on a workload it does not control.
premise.reportedComponent: pkg/reconciler workload reconcilers (ConstructRoleStatus / CheckWorkloadReady / Reconciler) + internal/controller/workloads rolebasedgroup_controller
premise.patchedComponent: same: pkg/reconciler/common.go checkWorkloadClaimable applied in all four workload reconcilers
premise.evidence: On base 0821cb5b the three P0 unit tests fail (ConstructRoleStatus reports ready=1 from a foreign-UID workload; CheckWorkloadReady returns true) and the envtest spec observes the persisted RBG Ready=True with readyReplicas=1 (results/base/*, results/envtest-base.txt). The base controller log additionally shows the workload apply failing with 'Only one reference can have Controller set to true' — SSA can never take over the leftover, so the false Ready persisted for the whole GC window (results/envtest-base-controller-evidence.txt).
match: P0: must not report readiness inherited from a foreign-UID leftover workload

findings.claim: While any role's workload is terminating (e.g. stuck behind a finalizer), removing another role from the RBG spec must still clean up the removed role's workload. On the PR head the claimable check returns ErrWorkloadNotClaimable for a terminating workload even when the RBG owns it, aborting Reconcile at Step 8 so the Step 9 cleanup never runs.
match: F1: removing a role still cleans up its workload while another role's workload is stuck terminating
F1-control: removing a role cleans up its workload when nothing is stuck

findings.claim: An orphan carrying the group-name label is claimable, so ConstructRoleStatus still reads its readyReplicas before adoption has happened. If a later fix gates status on actual control, this test flips to red and must be inverted.

GetWorkloadName truncates to 63 chars, so two roles sharing a 52-char prefix map to one workload name, and the orphan branch of checkWorkloadClaimable inspects only the group-name label — role A's orphan is claimable at role B's slot. If a later fix also checks the role label, the NoError assertion flips to red.

liveNote: L3 (live cluster) was intentionally skipped per the review-round instructions: a reachable cluster was observed (2 aliyun nodes, v1.36.2) but the debate setup restricts stage 2 to unit + integration layers. The e2e orphan-adoption case added by the PR itself passed in the PR's own CI run, covering the real-cluster adoption path.
